text:
Kailer Yamamoto came back for Utah on Nov. 11 after more than a week out, and André Tourigny has handed him more than he had before. His ice time over the last ten games is up almost five minutes a night, and over 18 minutes in four of the five games since his return, with three assists in the overtime loss to San Jose (the team posted a clip of the patience on one of them).

He has 12 points in 14 games, mostly assists, and the five-on-five numbers are the best on the team: Utah takes 65% of the expected goals with him on, more than ten points better than without him. His own goals lag. He has 3 on 5.1 expected, which is why our numbers have him as due: he keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances.

This fits last season too. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.0 wins, 98th percentile at taking chances away, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a setup man who does his damage off the rush. Watch whether the bigger role sticks now that he's healthy.
